newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds dragged down by falling U.S. bonds.
newsitem.headline: Bunds dragged down by falling U.S. bonds.

text.p: German Bunds fell to major losses on Wednesday, dragged down by a steep decline in U.S. Treasuries, and dealers were at a loss to predict the market's movements over the coming days as volatility has increased.

March Bund futures fell as low as 99.88, down 91 basis points from Tuesday's close, before clawing back some territory to trade at 100.10 at 1600 GMT. Dealers said the contract had strong technical support at 99.50.
The yield on the benchmark, 6.25 percent April Bund rose to 5.86 percent from 5.76 percent at Tuesday's close.
Nevertheless, the fate of Bunds would remain tied to Treasuries, dealers said.

"It makes no sense to try to withstand a fall in U.S. bonds," one dealer said. Depending on the level at which Treasuries close trade today, the Bund future could be anywhere between 99.50 and 100.50 on Thursday, the dealer said.
The U.S. market shrugged off a 0.4 percent rise in the U.S. producer price index in November, above forecasts for a 0.3 percent rise.
Dealers said they were now waiting for the U.S. consumer prices for November, with economists polled by Reuters expecting a rise of 0.3 percent month-on-month and a 3.0 percent rise year-on-year.
